**Step 1 - Scene:** This is not really a meal; it is a single whole apple (red-yellow, glossy) on a white ceramic plate, photographed from above at an oblique angle. Nearby, at the bottom edge, are other white dishes/cups that are not part of this food.

**Step 2 - Ruler:** The white plate is a triangular/fan-shaped dish, roughly 22 cm across its longest undistorted width. Area ≈ 3.14 × (11)² ≈ 380 cm² for a round equivalent; the actual dish is smaller in usable area, so I treat it as roughly 300 cm².

**Step 3 - Items:** One whole apple (fresh, raw).

**Step 4 - Area:** The apple covers about 12% of the plate's visible area (roughly 7 cm across × 8 cm tall in projection, ~40 cm²), so about 13% of the plate.

**Step 5 - Volume:** An apple of about 7–8 cm diameter has a volume of roughly 180–200 ml (it is nearly spherical, so volume ≈ 4/3·π·r³ with r ≈ 3.7 cm gives ~210 ml; I take ~190 ml since it is slightly flattened).

**Step 6 - Grams:** A whole apple is a solid piece, not a loose pile, so the bulk density of cut fruit does not really apply. Use the actual density of apple flesh (~0.85 g/ml) → about 160 g. A medium apple typically weighs 150–180 g, which is consistent.

**Step 7 - Energy:** Raw apple ≈ 52 kcal/100 g → 160 g × 0.52 ≈ 83 kcal.

**Step 8 - Sanity check:** A single medium apple at ~160 g and ~80–85 kcal is plausible and matches typical values. It is a snack-sized item, not a full meal, so the small total is expected.

**Result:** About 160 g of apple, about 83 kcal.
